# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **three levels of independently committable and
> independently verifiable tasks**.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates in the body of RFC-039 are the sole authority. This document
> is responsible only for breaking the work down to an executable granularity and registering
> conflicts that have not yet been decided.

## Purpose and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with the phase sequence in RFC-039                       |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, which can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                   |

**Reserved numbering (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also reserved (2026-11-25). All three have had no
corresponding entries since the WBS was established—the complete history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` (this can be verified with
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no
repository-wide references either. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that phase was divided into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's numbering is aligned
with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for the tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
justification for the phase order (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered level-2/level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—**owning phase** (the P to which it truly belongs, which may differ from
the section containing it) and **blocks mainline**; `pending scheduling` is no longer the default
state, and an unmarked task is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique across the
entire document** (tasks on separate tracks use a track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closeout registration convention (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four
items—the task ID, status, **short implementation commit hash** (7 characters), and issue number
(only when applicable)—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion items** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not
write the fix, the criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a
dashboard, not a process chronicle. **Do not write decision labels or restate conclusions**: “user
decision A/B/C,” “option A,” “final implementation is…”—none of these belong in this table. The
dashboard answers only “is it complete?”; see commit messages and the RFC-039 decision register for
decisions and results.

**Short hashes are determined after push**: a closeout row records the short hash on `origin/dev`
after the push completes; the order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the
closeout row** (see “commit number is obtained after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closeout commit itself carries no hash—a
self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains numbers only**: the level-1/level-2/level-3 counts in
`Purpose and Scope` contain only the current values; increment/decrement history (`+1 = …`) does not
go in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Resolution                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 had no implementation steps**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform that split; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains one mention of `annotations.rs`, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                                   | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                         |
| G2  | **The three ownership sites for the `include!` refactor had no implementation**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; S7 in `06` also lists it. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) **does not contain `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                                 | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 in this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here    |
| G3  | **Three parallel lists of CI scripts coexisted**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists four checks under entirely different names; `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least nine new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | The unified list appears in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table         |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` argues for deletion                                                                                                                                                                                                | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision register C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                        |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 goal**: RFC-039 and the index in this directory previously said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | This has converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Reason for adding P0**: the three prohibitions—no fabrication, no endless filling, and no patching
when a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established before
work begins; otherwise, work would already be under way by the time P1 revives tests and starts
adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`, which is precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Bugs (Minimal Approach)

Source: the bug-fix half of §Implementation Points S3 in [02](02-stage-contract.md) + **the
2026-10-07 silent-discard-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, user decision on 2026-10-11)**: if this track or any later
> phase discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure
> / B silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and uncontrolled resource use** (crashes, stack
> exhaustion, silently returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactoring**,
> but all four requirements must be met: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must exist first
> and actually be red); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that
> previously compiled successfully and ran correctly (they must not become failures, and their
> existing diagnostic codes/text/exit codes must not be removed or changed); ③ register it in the
> same commit (this row identifies the error class + the phase revision note + the PR
> mandatory-block “Error type” line); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review
> the diff. **The three classes D user-visible semantics / E external contract table / F RFC-level
> design changes must still be decided first. See
> [07 §Semantic-correction routing criteria](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria and
> A–F allowlist; **do not adopt “default super-refactor + post-hoc registration”** (the rationale is
> in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be distinguished from regressions, and this
> conflicts with the absence of C5′ and the prohibition on any relaxation).

**Acceptance**: the bug criterion turns green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn it red
again**. **Risk**: adding E4018 to multi-file paths is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is forbidden);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate as their criteria. **Risk**: the
new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change, so the corpus differential baseline and CHANGELOG
must be updated in sync.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 does not have to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**; the rest
> (2.1 IR verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can
> proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping correctness bugs (such as `Sorted(3)` passing silently) must
> not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure work. 3.3 (panic-to-diagnostic conversion) has no
> prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Auto-Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted on 2026-10-02;
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**; it is separate from P10 S5 “lower the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust's
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must entirely precede P4**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surface of
all four refactoring phases; reversing the order = redoing the same deletions and baseline updates
on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and grammar branches                                        | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexer convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                               |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 AST dead variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branch of `collect_exports`         | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→real `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**; the pub branch will be moved verbatim into the new file)                                                                                                                                        |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slim down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| The `Public` modifier in `semantic_tokens`                          | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `ir_gen`'s ignoring of `is_pub` bindings                            | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (SSA-ify `ir_gen.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase changes them directly, but **P6's hard acceptance criterion requires no diff in `src/std/`** (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; direct-drive test exceptions under `tests/` are described in the P6 hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Incidental benefit**: 029g deletes the dead `env.exports` table (filled by the producer and
consumed nowhere in the repository) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4's 4.3
obligation ledger has one fewer “produced but unconsumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavioral changes must have its red criterion land
   before code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (pub items were previously always
   exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, they must be replaced with
   equivalent new cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse errors + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; the IR snapshot is expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with 3.4 at the file level (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must
be sequential and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g
track does not depend on 3.4; implementers may choose which to do first based on the context at
hand.

> **Commit comparison (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter + the
> main-chain/constraint row) was folded into `97071c81b` together with RFC-039's D56 during a
> parallel-stream cleanup of the working tree—the commit message records “3.4
> additional-registration + D57/D58 decisions recorded” and does not mention this track. History is
> not rewritten; following the existing precedent (`d5b18390`, see the P2 closeout note), it is
> registered in place as evidence for later bisection.

Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` in `main.yx` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (old behavior was unsuccessful: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by a runtime failure or silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—obtain the declaration-time formal names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` according to the definition unit's qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (the candidate ↔ mixed-IR-name ↔ formal-name three vectors are in the same order, and come from the same source as typecheck's injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table, rather than two bare names. **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; according to
measurement, 5.3 **did not move it**, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines long—they
add navigation cost, reduce cohesion, and provide zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62's end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> one set of compile-time items. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **only input** for slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is **pure
> determination** (the two sides are equal after normalization; no type variables are bound);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value
> environment/single-value pinning/Γ equations); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (this
> holds for closed, open, and recursive terms); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence
> interface and do not establish another one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not
> merely that the subphase names have been completed.**

> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 decision → A.C3; determination-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 is toward typecheck→mono, d is toward types/solver→sema); C.2 may
> run in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B / 6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D implementation

> and may depend on the typed exit in 6.9.3. **The P7 gate = the exits of A/B/C; D does not block.**

> **Prerequisite for A.C3: F4 decision (A was decided on 2026-11-16; measurement)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation layer `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can hold `k-1`. **The
> decision is changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open term enters `deferred` and is normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (only mono is allowed; C-1 reconstruct from a second field and
> C-2 reconstruct from the IR both break the single representation/evaluator, C-3 = A); **F4-T
> termination** (naive firing causes the recursion chain to hit `max_depth` and E3005; T-a
> conditionally fire inside the instance / T-b bounded firing + revert to the original at the
> boundary / T-c add a termination layer or modify the specification). **Measure first, then decide;
> before measurement, “A is already implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User
> (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; implement C3 as a separate task, and do
> not claim that I4 is complete.**

> **Prerequisite for B.d: determination-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies
> that “a determination point first follows the unified procedure; after unified failure, defeq may
> be used, but the partial bindings produced by the unified attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq be attempted only when both sides are ground (no unbound variables);
> what are the snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; do unify and defeq share one budget or
> have separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify continues to be responsible for
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only determines equivalence and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **First provide the
> protocol and production call graph, then write code**; the wiring contract in 6.9.3c was already
> wasted on two rounds by assuming that `can_assign` was the determination point, and
> `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instances.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① corpus/IR snapshot
> zero drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected integration tests; ③
> error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point / code registry changes); ④ behavioral
> changes classified under D59 and red first, then green. **Wiring tasks additionally require**:
> evidence from the production call graph (which production entry point, how many paths, which path
> is reachable); a unit-test path must not be presented as user-reachable; rollback and budget
> require measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537 (Class D, silent discard of
> proof-function parameter refinement; do not fix before the decision, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not

> covers only module-internal cases), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 was

> MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—three sites

> entry-point wiring + C2c temporary-workaround removal; red→green, 402/402, function-table

**Hard acceptance** (**revised on 2026-10-27, following 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive modified code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change, but
each modification must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be
deleted, and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral fix** batch
(new diagnostic codes + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with a separate decision.

> **Revision relationship**: the original wording (2026-10-26 decision ②) was
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, treating all of `tests/` as requiring a zero diff; this
> revision **changes only direct-drive test files from “zero diff” to “may be changed but must
> register file / line count / reason”**, while **the zero-diff requirement for the corpus layer
> (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`) remains
> unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs` was changed, by **3
> lines** (2 instances of `assert_format_eq` changing `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), with the
> reason = the expected type name in the assertion must be synchronized when the changed spelling
> requires it; no tests were deleted and no assertions were weakened. See “P6 6.1 Name-Normalization
> Closeout.”

- [x] **7.0 Pure-move split** (6 level-3 tasks)

> **7.0 design basis and boundaries**: the target layout comes from the directory tree and migration
> table in [01-routing](01-routing.md)—`middle/ir/ir_gen.rs` → `middle/lower/`,
> `sema/inference/expressions.rs` → `sema/infer/` (the call-resolution family `call/`). This batch
> **only performs pure moves**, with the acceptance criterion being “zero semantic diff apart from
> paths” (manual review of each file) + C1 snapshot zero-diff. It does not conflict with RFC-039's
> rejection of alternative A “split files only, without changing the paradigm”: what was rejected is
> using a move **in place of** paradigm work; this batch is a **prerequisite** for paradigm
> work—7c.1's `lower/synth.rs` depends on the `lower/` directory being in place, and 7d.1's
> method-level split of `generate_call_expr_ir` is performed on the smaller files after the move.
> The expressions side follows the decision (split only the call-resolution family; `statements.rs`
> remains in place); the wholesale `inference/ → infer/` rename and merging statements belong to the
> full migration, are outside this batch, and require a separate design round after P7. `synth.rs`
> is a new boundary, not a move, and is assigned to 7c.1. Survey baseline (2026-11-12): `ir_gen.rs`
> has 9,804 lines and 148 methods, with its body in a single `impl AstToIrGenerator` block
> (approximately 9,250 lines); `expressions.rs` has 6,825 lines and 93 methods, with its body in a
> single `impl ExpressionInferrer` block (approximately 6,280 lines); the largest methods are
> `infer_call_expr` at 1,671 lines and `generate_call_expr_ir` at 866 lines (the latter is the
> target of 7d.1).

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and a missed consumer silently changes
associativity (no error, only a changed parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and the operator-property cross-check test; every new operator must enter both the table
and the cross-check test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or the
> action code refers backward to `sema`, `check-boundary.py` will block it.

report-only are turned hard in P9 (changing “report” to “fail”)—existing violations (parallel

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (user decision on 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (the multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and the performance baseline) can
> proceed in parallel with P3. Correctness bugs must not be blocked by criterion-infrastructure
> work; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all three layers
> of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Bug criteria must be **written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to be fossilized as “established behavior” in the phase table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list appears in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker splitting modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise regressions cannot be bisected to a specific location                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = the exits of phases A/B/C in 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completed 6.9.4), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface and must not establish a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The snapshot baseline in 9.5 and the `pub(crate)` leak count in 9.3 take their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                        | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC-039)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | The file sets are disjoint: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs. `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                            |
| B                                            | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| C                                            | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| D                                            | 4.4 (proof-layer wrap-up) ∥ the entire P6 line                                     | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| E                                            | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| F                                            | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 can be developed in parallel) | The snapshot baseline in 9.5 must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| G                                            | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | The file sets are disjoint (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies the two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; there are no pairwise intersections) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (same
batch files B6/E5); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track's pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be sequential).

**New internal documentation constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly sequential; 7.0
→ 7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly sequential (7.0 is the pure-move batch preceding P7), and the `Phi` arm in
7b must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” while rules are
  “prior judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor is required”; only D0–D4's
  review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the original G3 gap with three coexisting
  lists prevented closure. This merged table assigns each of the 10 active scripts to one phase (9.8
  was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), making report-only status and the hard-transition point
  explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to execute after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactoring means redoing the same deletions on the new
  grammar, new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as 7e's incorporation of
  `2315`/`2341` and S4's incorporation of RFC status corrections.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker splitting would exceed the granularity at which work can be
  rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero call-site changes” as hard acceptance**—the split must be independently
  revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  must not be rolled back” and lacks a recording requirement for “what was fixed.” **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and the defect
  description, as evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames; missing one silently
  changes associativity.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, while the deletion
  action remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to a “separate issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was incorporated as 7e.3; `2315` was rechecked on 2026-11-28 and
  found to be an audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no
  throw/try/catch), 7e.2 was cancelled, and the exception remnants were assigned to P10 S6.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

## Conflict Register: All Resolved

> **The original “Conflict Register” C1–C8 and the open questions in each document have all
> converged into the [RFC-039 Decision Register](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** No unresolved item remains in this document. The correspondence is itemized below:

| Original number | Issue                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                           | **Revive it** (the premise of P1 is to revive tests that contain real assertions); P8 no longer deletes this file (Pratt is retained)                                          |
| C2              | The “grammar-driven” commitment vs. table-driven parsing                            | **Fallback approach**: retain Pratt + one declarative precedence table + mutual cross-checking of the two `BinOp` implementations (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and the S1 classification               | **S1 is classified as C6** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”        |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` allowlist                                        | **No allowlist**; the difference must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                                  |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions have not been verified | **P4's 4.2.7 explicitly lists verification as required**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                   |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                                 | **The wasm-path bug fix is incorporated into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                            |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                                  | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c); see D21                                                                                                                                       |
| C8              | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                             | **Fix it + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`); see D17                                     |
